title: Sanitize FFI/JNI crypto bindings and introduce ABI-stable abstraction layer
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Address a class of brittle native bindings and JNI/FFI uses that couple the runtime to specific OpenSSL/JWT/SAML library ABIs. Goal: reduce supply-chain and runtime risk by introducing an ABI-stable C shim/adapter and replacing direct JNI/FFI callsites with a well-tested abstraction. This enables rolling upgrades of crypto libs and safer backports of OpenSSL without process-level symbol collisions.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a small, documented C shim (redistributable) that exposes a stable minimal crypto adapter surface used by runtime components
All existing JNI/FFI callsites removed or migrated to the adapter layer in production services
Regression tests and CI fuzz harness validate SAML XML parsing and JWT verification against the golden corpus
No increase in median p99 latency for token verification paths (>5% threshold) after migration
Automated compatibility check added to release pipeline that detects OpenSSL/JNI symbol conflicts during image build
steps: Audit repository to enumerate JNI/FFI callsites and transitive native symbols (tooling: nm/objdump + runtime symbol scan)
Design minimal C shim API covering: TLS init/config, sigverify (RSA/EC), HMAC, random, and a limited SAML XML verification helper
Implement shim in a small portable component with explicit symbol prefixes to avoid collisions
Create language bindings: thin Rust and Java adapters that call the shim instead of linking OpenSSL directly
Introduce CI job: build shim with multiple OpenSSL versions and verify no duplicate global symbols
Migrate one non-critical service end-to-end as a canary and run traffic-preserving comparison
Run fuzzing campaign (OSS-Fuzz-like harness) against SAML XML parser and JWT edge-cases; capture failures and triage to fixes
Roll out library adapters to remaining services with phased deploy and automated rollback on errors
rollout_plan: Phase 0: merge shim and adapters behind feature flag in test branch; run unit+integration tests
Phase 1: canary deploy to sandbox service (low traffic) for 72 hours, collect telemetry
Phase 2: promote to one customer-facing non-critical region with 10% traffic shift
Phase 3: full rollout for token path across runtime after 7 days of stable metrics
Emergency rollback: revert to previous artifacts and re-enable direct linking if symbol conflict or critical failure detected
test_plan: Unit tests covering shim API semantics and error paths
Integration tests exercising Java/Rust bindings in CI against multiple OpenSSL versions (1.1.1, 3.0, 3.1-dev)
Performance baseline: measure token verification p50/p95/p99 before and after migration
Fuzz harness for SAML XML parser with corpus from field logs (sanitized) and synthetic edge cases
Cross-build tests in release matrix to detect symbol collisions at container image stage
